chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding the one in Ihram who clips a nail: He said, 'He should give in charity with a palmful of food.' He said, 'Two nails?' He said, 'Two palmfuls.' I said, 'Three?' He said, 'Three palmfuls.' I said, 'Four?' He said, 'Four palmfuls.' I said, 'Five?' He said, 'Upon him is blood (of a slaughtered animal) to be spilled. So if he were to cut ten or more than that, there would not be upon him except for blood (of a slaughtered animal) to be spilled.'

key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood (referring to the blood of a sacrificed animal)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation (fidya) for clipping nails while in Ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the graduated fidya for clipping nails while in Ihram, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition of proportional expiation based on the quantity of the transgression. It establishes a clear distinction where minor infractions are compensated with food (sadaqah), while more significant violations require the slaughter of an animal (dam), illustrating the juristic principle of balancing ritual purity with practical atonement. The text highlights the Imam's precise legal reasoning, moving from material compensation to blood sacrifice as the severity of the act increases.
